#1852. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1851. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1850. Arsenal transfer news: David Ornstein drops interesting update on Eli Junior Kroupi ahead of January

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 06:57

Arsenal could face imminent disappointment in their pursuit of AFC Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with David Ornstein providing an update on the 19-year-old's future.

The Gunners have been monitoring the Frenchman after his impressive performances, but a move for him in the January transfer window is now looking increasingly unlikely.

Ornstein has also suggested that Kroupi could favour a move away from the Premier League when he eventually leaves the Vitality Stadium.

In a recent The Athletic Q&A, Ornstein downplayed the prospect of the Cherries sanctioning a January departure, saying the club has little financial incentive to sell midway through the campaign.

The forward is under contract until 2030, meaning the Cherries are in a strong negotiating position and can afford to wait until the summer before considering significant offers.

Ornstein also highlighted that Kroupi only made his first appearance of the season on October 25th after an injury lay-off, with Bournemouth keen to benefit from his contributions during the remainder of the campaign.

Perhaps more significantly for Arsenal, the ever-reliable journalist suggested that the teenager could prefer a move abroad rather than another Premier League club.

Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona have both been heavily linked, with Ornstein indicating that the information available to him points towards those destinations being more likely than a move within England.

He did acknowledge that an exceptional financial offer from a Premier League club could change the situation, but his expectation is that Bournemouth would be more receptive to a sale next summer.

Ornstein's update represents a significant complication for Arsenal, who could now need to explore alternative attacking targets if they want to strengthen in January.

Kroupi's contract situation means Bournemouth have little reason to entertain offers, while the player's reported preference for moving abroad further weakens the Gunners' position.

Antonio Nusa could therefore become a more realistic alternative for Gunners boss Mikel Arteta.

The RB Leipzig winger is another young attacking talent attracting Premier League interest, with Arsenal previously linked alongside Tottenham and reportedly confident of competing for his signature.

Nusa would not necessarily provide the same centre-forward option as Kroupi, but his ability to operate out wide could address another area where Arsenal need greater depth.

Ultimately, Kroupi remains an exciting long-term target, but the combination of Bournemouth's stance and his apparent preference for a move abroad suggests Arsenal may have to be patient or turn their attention elsewhere in January.

#1848. When will Mauricio Pochettino arrive at Manchester United? Travel plans revealed after final USMNT fixture

The dawn of the Mauricio Pochettino era is upon us, with the Argentine having taken to the dugout with the United States for the final time on Tuesday evening.

Pochettino is returning to the Premier League for a fourth time, replacing Michael Carrick as head coach of Manchester United.

He is facing a sizeable rescue mission, with Man United languishing in 18th in the Premier League having won just one of their first ten matches. He faces a tricky start, too, with Liverpool, Sporting CP, and Brentford on the docket for his first matches in charge.

While Carrick was formally dismissed last week, after the Man Utd hierarchy held crisis talks regarding his future in Monaco, Pochettino has been delayed in actually starting his new role.

He first had to see out one last international break with the United States national team, which involved a two-legged tie against Haiti, before returning to England.

Pochettino’s term as Manchester United manager will officially begin today, November 18, 2026, as confirmed in a club statement last week.

That start date was chosen to allow him to lead the United States national team through their two Concacaf Nations League matches this international break, a two-legged tie against Haiti. The second of those two legs kicked off at midnight on Tuesday night for UK viewers.

The Argentine was set to travel to Manchester immediately after the match, on a private jet laid on by United. That will see him touch down in the north-west on Wednesday morning.

Pochettino is expected to head straight from the airport to Carrington, where he will throw himself headlong into preparing for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

Some of his backroom staff arrived on location in Manchester ahead of Pochettino, however, laying some groundwork before the head coach’s own arrival.

#1847. Ashley Young names Premier League star Manchester United should sign to replace Bruno Fernandes

Ashley Young reckons it is time for Manchester United to move on from Bruno Fernandes and feels there is a Premier League star who should be signed to replace him.

Fernandes has consistently been the Red Devils’ best player since joining from Sporting in January 2020.

However, at 32 years old and with new manager Mauricio Pochettino arriving this week, doubts over whether Fernandes will remain the focal point of the team are being raised.

The United captain is into the final few months of his contract and has reportedly rejected two offers of a new deal.

The club has the option to extend his current contract by another month, which would prevent Fernandes leaving on a free transfer in the summer, but he could still be sold in 2027 if that option is taken up.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Former Red Devils man Young reckons it is time to move on from Fernandes and thinks the man to replace him is Nottingham Forest and England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The former Wolves star turns 27 in January and Young feels now is the time for Manchester United to make him their main man, replacing Fernandes.

‘He’s been unbelievable for the club, the standout performer,’ Young said of Fernandes on Overlap Daily. ‘But there’s been so much that’s come about. He’s turned down another contract, we’re hearing.

‘You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year. Age is nothing but a number, but he’s not in his peak. I wouldn’t say past it, but he’s getting older now.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘For me, I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White. I’m just throwing that name out there. But you’re thinking a number 10 and you want to build a team around a player.

‘He’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got in the England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club. And I think he’s someone that Manchester United need, in his peak years.

‘I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say I can play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that.’

As much as signing new players will be on the agenda for the new Manchester United manager, getting rid of unwanted squad members may be the bigger test.

Gary Neville feels there needs to be a significant cull over the next few transfer windows, with some big names ideally being axed at the end of the season.

‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, [Matthijs] De Ligt would go, [Noussair] Mazraoui would go, [Mason] Mount would go, first wave next summer. [Marcus] Rashford if you can, and [Joshua] Zirkzee,’ the former full-back said on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at [Luke] Shaw, [Harry] Maguire, [Diogo] Dalot, Bruno [Fernandes], that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on [Carlos] Baleba and [Andrey] Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1846. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1843. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday night, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1842. Liverpool transfer news: Reds join Barcelona race for Brazilian defender amid Van Dijk doubt

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04

Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved. The Dutch defender’s contract runs until the end of the season and he has yet to reach an agreement over an extension, while Liverpool are monitoring the market.

While the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes. With his contract running until the end of the season, Van Dijk has no renewal agreement in progress and can sign a pre-contract agreement from January.

With the situation of the Dutch defender unresolved, Liverpool have entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem.

According to Sports Illustrated, Liverpool have sent scouts to follow the rise of Arthur Dias closely and are now assessing the possibility of buying him from Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is one of the breakout stars of Brazilian football in 2026 and is being watched by several European clubs.

Barcelona’s interest in Arthur Dias is long-standing, as being left-footed and comfortable playing out from the back are qualities missing from manager Hansi Flick’s squad. Van Dijk, who is right-footed but also plays on the left side of central defence, would leave a gap for Liverpool to fill should he depart.

The Brazilian centre-back has a contract until December 2028 and has already seen a Tottenham Hotspur offer of £18m (€21m) rejected by Athletico Paranaense. The club’s board believes Arthur Dias should only be released for an offer of at least £25.5m (€30m) because of his high potential.

So far, Liverpool have made no formal approach to Athletico Paranaense for the young defender, but the competition is not limited to Barcelona.

Clubs such as Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also monitoring Arthur Dias, who gained international visibility with his first two call-ups to the Brazil national team in the post-World Cup international breaks.

Brazilian aside, Liverpool’s number four has no guaranteed future at Anfield. Despite his idol status and undisputed place in the starting line-up under manager Andoni Iraola, Van Dijk has no advanced talks with the club’s directors over his stay, with moves towards an extension expected to gather pace at the turn of the year.

The captain himself admitted in a recent interview that he plans to stay at Liverpool, but has no news on his situation.

The Spanish manager is in favour of Van Dijk staying, as the Dutchman is not only a leadership figure in the dressing room but also a pillar of the defensive system, having won 75% of his duels in this season’s Premier League.

In that context, AC Milan have emerged as one of the clubs interested in the 35-year-old defender. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is an admirer of the Dutchman and believes he can make a difference to Ruben Amorim’s project through his experience and technical quality.

#1841. New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino reacts to ‘city is blue’ comment with six-word promise

Mauricio Pochettino has said to “give him time” to make Manchester United the dominant club in the city again as he prepares to start work.

Pochettino will take charge of Man United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday after being appointed to succeed Michael Carrick, who was sacked last week with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s return to club management has been delayed after being allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States national team.

His last game ended in a 2-0 win for USA against Haiti in Cincinnati during the early hours on Wednesday (UK time) to wrap up an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

AC Milan forward Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a spectacular overhead kick and teenager Julian Hall doubled the hosts’ lead before half-time.

After bidding an emotional farewell to the USA supporters inside the stadium, Pochettino immediately turned his attentions to the task at hand with Man United and the rivalry with Manchester City.

Told by former Man City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue” in the TNT Sports US studio after the game, Pochettino responded: “You will see. Give me time.

“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenalin you want to feel.

“We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.”

Pochettino heads to Old Trafford tasked with steering Man United out of the relegation zone before he can target winning titles and eventually usurping Man City as the dominant team in the city.

United have not been crowned Premier League champions since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, with the legendary Scotsman final season being the last time the club finished above their neighbours in the table.

Additional reporting by Press Association.

#1839. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1837. How Manchester United could line up in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game vs Liverpool as big calls made

The Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United is officially underway, and his first game is just days away.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival, while the Argentine might be tempted to copy Michael Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back, instructing the Frenchman to tuck in and form a three-man defence in possession.

However, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach.

Yoro could therefore partner Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence to give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu is a doubt after being sent home from international duty with Denmark, but is said to be winning his battle to be fit for the Anfield trip and could replicate what Antonee Robinson did for Pochettino at left-back.

With the USA, Pochettino had settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

Pochettino’s immediate issue with the Man United squad will be the fact that there is no clear candidate as a holding midfielder. The injured Baleba does well at screening the backline, but his strengths rely on driving forward with the ball.

Tielemans could play the box-to-box role alongside Mainoo, offering experience during the transition to Pochettino’s ideal approach.

That is because club captain Bruno Fernandes is clearly the Red Devils’ best player, which merits his inclusion.

#1836. Man Utd full-back facing major contract decision as Mauricio Pochettino plots defensive overhaul

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:17, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 07:17

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to make several changes to his Manchester United squad, with the defence expected to be a major priority over the coming transfer windows.

Noussair Mazraoui is among those whose long-term future at Old Trafford remains uncertain, despite previously being highly regarded by the club.

The Argentine is keen to assess the Morocco international in person before deciding whether to make a new contract a priority.

Mazraoui is attracting interest from clubs in both Italy and Saudi Arabia, but Pochettino wants to take a closer look at the right-back over the coming weeks before reaching a verdict on his future, according to new reports.

The 29-year-old is contracted to United until the summer of 2028, with the club also holding an option to extend his deal by a further year.

Consequently, neither party is in immediate danger of running out of time to agree fresh terms, and there is no urgency to conclude negotiations.

However, Mazraoui has endured an injury-disrupted start to the campaign, making just five Premier League appearances so far.

United are understood to be planning a 'defensive overhaul' across the next few transfer windows, although the former Bayern Munich defender could avoid the significant changes expected elsewhere in the backline.

His versatility is a major asset, having featured at right-back, left-back and centre-back, while he remains viewed as a potentially important part of the project at Old Trafford.

Nevertheless, Mazraoui will need to impress Pochettino before the manager decides whether to commit to him for the longer term.

United's defensive problems have plagued the club for several seasons, and simply making one or two adjustments is unlikely to provide the necessary solution.

Pochettino, therefore, needs to take a wider view of the backline, with multiple additions potentially required across the defensive positions.

Left-back should be a particularly important area of focus, while further reinforcements at centre-back and right-back could also be needed depending on who survives the anticipated overhaul.

Mazraoui's ability to cover several positions could make him a useful squad member, but his injury record and contract situation mean that his future cannot be taken for granted.

Ultimately, Pochettino must establish which defenders can form part of his long-term plans before United commit significant resources to rebuilding their defence.

#1835. Who makes up Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff at Manchester United?

Manchester United have turned to Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager, and a new backroom staff will be joining him for his return to the Premier League.

After identifying ex-Tottenham boss Pochettino as the desired replacement for sacked head coach Michael Carrick, Man Utd quickly agreed personal terms - before approaching the USA to extract their target from a four-year contract only signed following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It has been reported that the total compensation package United will have to pay the US Soccer Federation could be north of £10million, once fees for Pochettino’s staff have been included.

Assistant manager Jesus Perez has worked with Pochettino since his first job in management, employed initially as an analyst at Espanyol in LaLiga.

After building a strong relationship with Pochettino, Spaniard Perez was promoted to No2 when the Argentine was appointed manager of Southampton in 2013, and has been his assistant at every job since.

Perez and Pochettino joked about the United job during the World Cup, with the former apparently very keen on working at Old Trafford.

There are four other members of staff likely to make the move across the Atlantic.

Miguel D’Agostino is a former team-mate of Pochettino’s, with the duo having played together at Newell’s Old Boys in their native Argentina.

Initially working as a scout for Pochettino at Espanyol, D’Agostino has also followed his compatriot from club to club since then.

Toni Jimenez is another to have worked with Pochettino at every club he has managed so far, plus the US national team. A goalkeeping coach, Jimenez first linked up with Pochettino in 2011 at Espanyol.

The penultimate member of coaching staff mentioned in reports has not been involved in Pochettino’s setup as long as the others, but has a very close relationship to the former Chelsea manager.

Sebastiano Pochettino is Mauricio’s son and started working within his father’s coaching team at Spurs. He has continued in his role as a sports scientist.

Silvia Tuya - full name Silvia Tuya Vinas - is a strength and conditioning coach, currently employed by the USMNT.

Tuya will become the first female coach of the men’s first team squad at Old Trafford, creating history ahead of a new chapter for Manchester United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical issue that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

#1830. Exclusive: Charlton boss Nathan Jones among managers objecting to FA rule change

Charlton manager Nathan Jones is among a number of head coaches in English football’s top four divisions to have objected to the reduction in how many yellow cards leads to a touchline ban.

Standard Sport understands that at a recent managers’ meeting, Jones and other head coaches from clubs among the 92 argued a 2023 change in FA rules towards stricter punishments for technical-area misconduct remains unjustified at a time when football managers have never faced greater pressure and volatility.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is incongruous with an increasingly demanding working environment.

Head coaches across the Premier League and EFL are understood to have this season been shown research that suggests managers’ behaviour usually improves once they reach three bookings.

Managers are regularly reminded of a variety of regulations including technical-area misconduct rules during meetings with the FA’s disciplinary teams, who often present research and statistics to contextualise changes to rules or emerging trends.

Ahead of the 2018-19 season, new rules were introduced to clean up touchline behaviour. Managers across the FA Cup, EFL, Carabao Cup, EFL Trophy and National League could receive yellow and red cards for the first time, with four yellows resulting in a one-match touchline ban.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is unreasonable

Premier League managers would receive only verbal cautions for “irresponsible behaviour” but then the top flight fell in line with the same level of punishment from 2019-20 onwards.

A further update was made ahead of the 2023-24 campaign when the FA launched a new ‘Participant Behaviour Charter’ as part of its ‘Love Football, Protect the Game’ campaign, developed alongside the Premier League, EFL, Women's Super League, Women's Championship, National League System (Steps 1–4), and PGMOL (now Pro Ref), with input from the League Managers Association (LMA) and Professional Footballers' Association (PFA).

The charter’s aim was to improve the image of the game and maintain a positive environment. Four yellows for a managerial suspension was reduced to three and has remained so ever since.

A new cut-off for technical-area cautions was introduced this season. Managers who receive their third technical-area booking after the 37th round of EFL league matches do not incur an immediate suspension. At that point an automatic one-match touchline ban is triggered only if a fourth yellow card is picked up in a subsequent game.

Compared with its peak, the number of technical-area cautions issued has decreased by 17 per cent since the introduction of the ‘Participation Behaviour Charter’, FA sources say.

Under the FA’s ‘Laws of the Game’, other staff and substitutes in a technical area can also be cautioned or even sent off.

In certain circumstances, managers and head coaches can get booked or sent off on behalf of the misconduct of others in their technical area if the fourth official reports a situation deserving of punishment to the referee but cannot verify who in the technical area committed the offence. In such situations, FA rules state cards can be shown to the “manager or most senior coach in [the technical] area”.

#1829. ‘Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty’ in Hull win as Premier League panel confirm incorrect offside

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel has voted unanimously that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 in the final match before the international break to go five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, it could have been a much more comfortable afternoon had Arsenal been given a penalty in the first half, when it was still goalless.

Kai Havertz went down in the box as he made a run in behind, having been pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

It was not initially seen by the officials but VAR advised the referee to stop play and consult the pitchside monitor.

Farai Hallam deemed that while Havertz had been fouled, he was in an offside position and therefore a free-kick was given to Hull.

The KMI panel have now confirmed that was the incorrect decision due to the foul taking place before Havertz became active.

All five members of the group voted that both the on-field decision and the outcome of the VAR intervention was wrong.

“Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz,” the panel explained.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

The panel added: “Being in an offside position, in itself, is not an offence.

“IFAB Law 11 says that a player in an offside position at the moment the ball is played or touched by a team-mate is only penalised on becoming involved in active play.

“If a player is fouled before becoming involved in active play, the foul is penalised as it has occurred before the offside offence. Therefore, in this instance, Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty.”

#1828. Mauricio Pochettino’s first six Manchester United games confirmed as brutal opener awaits

Manchester United are now preparing for life with Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.

Pochettino is believed to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford as he replaces Michael Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

The appointment of Pochettino has been driven by the Argentine's high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

His consistency of performing at the highest level of football across multiple leagues is an additional factor.

This will be Pochettino’s fourth spell in the Premier League, having previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea to varying levels of success.

As the latest new era at Old Trafford officially gets underway this next week, here is a everything to look forward to once Pochettino gets settled in...

As communicated in the official club statement, Pochettino’s start date is November 18 - after USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final second leg against Haiti.

He is expected to take charge of Man Utd training for the first time ahead of the showdown against Liverpool three days later.

United won both meetings with Liverpool last season, including a rare victory at Anfield, but Pochettino has not tasted victory at that ground since his Southampton days in the 2013-14 campaign.

As Man United travel to Lisbon, Portugal to face Sporting in their next Champions League assignment, it means it’s successive away games at the start of Pochettino’s tenure.

That means Brentford’s trip to Old Trafford on November 28 will serve as Pochettino’s first home game in charge.

We have already mentioned the first three, but it will be an interesting start for Pochettino as Newcastle (a) and Coventry (h) follow on from there in the Premier League.

The run concludes with a Champions League showdown against RB Leipzig on matchday six of this season’s league phase, where United will hope to put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the last-16.

It’s a mixed bag, Pochettino’s Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) spells offer cause for optimism.

At Southampton, Pochettino won one of his first six games and lost the other half. Meanwhile at Chelsea, the Argentine’s only two wins from his first six games were against newly promoted Luton and AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup.

That said, the Argentine oversaw four wins and a draw from his first six Spurs and PSG matches, before going one better with five wins from his first six matches in charge of the USMNT.
