#1827. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”

New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

This morning’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) confirms the No.1 centre-back target: Goncalo Inacio. Milan tried to snatch him from Sporting CP in August, but the Portuguese club repeatedly turned them down, having already sold Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest.

The Rossoneri haven’t abandoned the idea of ​​reuniting him with Amorim, and so in January they will make another attempt for the 25-year-old, who is eager to join a top club. However, a significant offer of at least €40m will be needed to convince Sporting.

#1825. Pochettino says ‘give me time’ as he prepares for Man Utd venture

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino defiantly stated, "You will see, give me time", before jetting off to begin his role as Manchester United head coach.

The Argentine rounded out his duties with the United States by beating Haiti 2-0 in the second leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory.

Following that fixture in Cincinnati, Pochettino flew straight to Manchester, then headed to the Red Devils' Carrington training complex.

United find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone after a tumultuous 2025-26 campaign thus far.

Club legend Michael Carrick was sacked after winning just one of 10 top-flight fixtures this season.

Former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea coach Pochettino was hired in his place, but wanted to see out the Haiti double-header.

Following the game, he was told by former USA and Manchester City midfielder DaMarcus Beasley that, "Manchester is blue, it always be blue".

Pochettino replied to the quip by saying: "You will see. Give me time.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 13, 2026

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time, it's adrenaline you want to feel. We need to add our common sense.

"We know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.

"The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us every day, we are a much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

United later posted a video on social media of Pochettino arriving, in which he said: "I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege, to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work."

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

Pochettino's first assignment could scarcely be a more difficult one, with United travelling to Anfield to face fierce north-west rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

He will be the first United boss to see his maiden league game in charge come against Liverpool.

This is the latest into a league season (MD11) that Liverpool and United have faced with one of the sides in the relegation zone since November 1972, when bottom side Man Utd beat league-leaders Liverpool 2-0 at Old Trafford.

#1824. Mauricio Pochettino has been told which FIVE Manchester United deals to complete before end of the season

Gary Neville has called on Mauricio Pochettino to complete an overhaul at Mancheter United, naming five players to be moved on by the end of the season.

The former Man United defender has also suggested another four or five players for the chopping block in a ‘second wave’ of exits.

Having previously commented that the Red Devils’ current defence would lead to relegation, it is no surprise that Neville focused on shipping out defenders.

But Neville fears that a complete reset of the Man Utd squad could take three seasons for Pochettino to complete.

Analysing the squad, Neville said on The Overlap’s Stick to United podcast: “Out of the defenders he’ll keep [Luke] Shaw because he knows him and he’ll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries and you’ll have to manage him.

“He’ll keep [Harry] Maguire because he’ll trust him and think he’s basically a soldier, someone who can do a job for him.

“He’ll keep [Leny] Yoro because he’ll think there’s something to work with. [Ayden] Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in.

“I’d keep Bruno [Fernandes], I’d keep Kobbie [Mainoo], I’d keep [Youri] Tielemans, [Mason] Mount would have to go.

“[Andrey] Santos - Mauricio may like him because he’s young, quite mobile, he’s aggressive, he might get something out of him. Him and [Carlos] Baleba will be in that middle bit. Mount’s the one that goes definitely, in that midfield section.”

Neville then went on to explain that Marcus Rashford’s wages meant he needed to be moved on at the ‘earliest opportunity’.

Manchester United transfer target Yasin Ayari appeared to pour cold water on any potential move to Old Trafford - before implying that he is keeping his options open.

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his decision to leave Manchester United in a statement, with Real Madrid expected to win the race to sign the highly-rated young winger.

The 16-year-old has played in United’s academy since 2020 and was expected to start appearing in the first team this season.

Until, that is, he made the shock decision to lodge a transfer request in September, amid reports he and his entourage were frustrated with his lack of first-team opportunities.

United worked hard to convince him to stay and offered him a new contract, but the player has not trained at the club for some time and is now expected to join Real Madrid. He will leave Old Trafford without having made a senior appearance.

After months of speculation as to where he might end up, Gabriel has now issued the clearest update yet on his situation, confirming his decision to leave United in a post to his Instagram page.

Speaking over clips of himself playing for the club, he said: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.

“Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

“To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

Furthermore, discussions over new deal for Riccardo Calafiori are on the horizon.

#1822. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

While the Three Lions were beaten on that occasion, it would be a favourable draw given they have won two of the last three meetings against the Dutch - including the Euro 2024 semi-final.

The simulator hasn't been as kind to France as they've been paired with Spain, a team they have lost to three times in a row since victory in the 2021 final.

In addition, the simulator has thrown up two other eye-catching fixtures with Norway taking on Germany, and Portugal continuing the defence of their crown against Belgium over two legs.

#1820. Mbappe should not be expected to defend, claims Real Madrid team-mate Rudiger

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Antonio Rudiger is baffled by criticism over Kylian Mbappe's defensive work rate.

Indeed, Rudiger feels it would be unfair to ask Mbappe, one of world football's great goalscorers, to "do my job".

Mbappe has already scored 17 goals and laid on three assists for Real Madrid this season. Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Barcelona's Raphinha (19) has netted more goals this term.

Since the start of 2026, Mbappe's tally of 30 goals is bettered by only Raphinha (33) and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane (41).

— Kylian Mbappé (@KMbappe) October 27, 2026

Last month, Mbappe surpassed 500 goal involvements in his club career, yet the Frenchman has still faced some criticism over a seeming lack of willingness to do the dirty work, something which has perplexed his Madrid team-mate Rudiger.

"Does it make sense for me to ask a man who has scored more than 80 or 90 goals in two years, and has now reached 100 goals for the club, to do my job? That makes no sense," Rudiger told The Athletic.

Rudiger then compared Mbappe to some star forwards of Madrid's recent past.

He added: "Let's go back to the past. What was it like in the era of Gareth Bale, [Karim] Benzema and Cristiano Ronaldo?

"Look at their success. We don't always need to talk about their defensive abilities."

Madrid sit second in LaLiga, three points behind leaders Barca. Jose Mourinho's side face Celta Vigo on Saturday.

#1819. Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners, relegation race, Golden Boot and more

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The 2026-27 Premier League season is just days away from resumption following the final international break of the year, and with it the return of some familiar faces.

Mauricio Pochettino is back in English football after a spell in international management, he has succeeded Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach. Meanwhile, Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

After 10 games of the campaign, both Man United and Palace are in the relegation zone. So will these appointment help to drag them out of the bottom three?

At the other end of the table, Arsenal have made a solid start to the defence of their Premier League crown, and appear to have a surprise challenger as confusion has set in around Manchester City.

Plenty of questions to be answered over the next six months, and the Standard Sport football reporters, Matt Verri, Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau, have had a go at predicting what is in store for the remainder of the season.

MV: Arsenal continue to look ruthlessly efficient and should be confident of defending their title. The defensive unit is absurdly good, the midfield depth is ridiculous, and it means the forwards only need to deliver a moment or two per match.

Even whey they are not at their best, Arsenal are just so difficult to beat. That is the case over 90 minutes and it should be the case over 38 matches again.

DS: No reason to change what I predicted at the beginning of the season, which was for Arsenal to win the Premier League title. If anything, the opening 10 rounds of games have made me more convinced the Gunners won’t be caught and will defend last season’s crown.

Arsenal fans may continue to worry about a lack of goals from their forwards, but their defence is on track to perform even better than last season’s, and that gives other challengers a daunting task to catch them. Arsenal could genuinely win the title by as many as 15 points.

ST: Arsenal were favourites to retain the Premier League title before the season started and that has not changed 10 games in.

Manchester City started the season with a perfect record, but their performances have begun to suffer, perhaps impacted by the looming threat of a potential points deduction.

Brighton will surely fall away, while the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea are capable but lacking consistency.

MV: Now it gets harder. Liverpool have not quite put it all together yet but there are signs that they will. I’ll go for them to just edge second ahead of Brighton, who have been superb this season but could fade slightly if they go deep in Europe as expected.

Chelsea have the firepower in attack to secure fourth and Unai Emery can work his magic to get Aston Villa into fifth.

DS: My top five, in order, back in August was Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, then Liverpool. That needs some revising.

Man City are difficult to predict because of the unknowns involved in their impending punishment for financial rule breaches, but they may just about hold on to second (pre-punishment). In third, there are signs Liverpool could come good, particularly if Alexander Isak can stay fit.

Brighton will drop from second but stay strong enough to finish in the Champions League in fourth. Chelsea in fifth — though their performances must improve.

ST: I think the teams who currently occupy the top five spots will all remain there, it is more a case of which position each team will finish. Arsenal will be champions, while I believe Brighton will slip to fifth when the going gets tough in the spring.

Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea are all interchangeable. But I think it will end up being City second, Liverpool third and Chelsea fourth.

MV: Assuming a resolution is reached this season, it is hard to see how Manchester City can avoid a sanction that leads to relegation. I predicted in the summer that Sunderland would go down and that has been reinforced over the first ten games. That squad looks stretched and sorely lacking in goals.

Thomas Frank was abysmal at Tottenham but can do enough to solidify things at Crystal Palace. Instead, Coventry will not quite have enough to stay up.

DS: Along with many others at the time, I predicted the three promoted teams to go straight back down. Even though Hull made a good start, Ipswich have been decent and Coventry seem to have turned a corner, I still expect those three to be weaker than Sunderland, Fulham, Crystal Palace and other strugglers as the many months progress. Coventry, Hull and Ipswich still.

ST: With so much time left in the season, it really is anyone’s guess who will get relegated. Just two points separate the Premier League’s bottom club Crystal Palace and 17th place Coventry, so if Thomas Frank gets it right, the Eagles can quickly pull away from danger.

I think Fulham, Nottingham Forest and Coventry are all capable of getting dragged into the relegation zone.

Sunderland, Forest and Coventry will be the three to go down.

MV: Thierno Barry gets enough chances in front of goal to challenge, while Alexander Isak is starting to show why Liverpool were so determined to sign him. However, it is hard not to be boring. Even with the circus surrounding City, Erling Haaland will almost certainly secure another Golden Boot.

Joao Pedro would be the one I might have backed to challenge him, but injury has stalled his challenge.

DS: Why would it be anyone other than Erling Haaland? It says a lot that even after the Norwegian was criticised in some circles for failing to score in City’s last two league games, the defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest, he is still sitting pretty on top of the leaderboard with nine goals in 10 league games.

The Golden Boot simply won’t be won by anyone else.

ST: It’s the boring answer but in a league lacking natural goalscsorers, Erling Haaland is the obvious pick. The Norwegian has been off the boil in recent weeks, but he always finds his way back into form.

No one knows where the back of the net is quite like Haaland. It’s that simple.

#1818. Pictured: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at airport before starting Manchester United role

Mauricio Pochettino has been pictured arriving in the UK for the first time as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine flew straight from the United States in the early hours of Wednesday morning and the Gulfstream G700 he was believed to be on was spotted landing at Manchester airport shortly before midday.

It was announced last week that the former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss was making a return to the Premier League, succeeding Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

However, the 54-year-old’s start to his fourth spell in English football was delayed as he finished up commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), overseeing an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals in his last game in charge.

Now after touching down in the UK, Pochettino can now take the next step in his career.

“I am ready [to return],” he told the Telegraph. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino is expected to head to Carrington immediately as he settles into his new role as Man United head coach, with the focus already shifting to his first game in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

#1817. Xabi Alonso facing new Chelsea team selection dilemma after Emi Martinez fitness boost

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso may have a selection headache on his hands after Emi Martinez returned to action.

Martinez played the full 90 minutes as Argentina thumped Costa Rica 7-0, producing two saves in a comfortable outing for what was his first outing since sustaining his jaw injury against Everton.

The goalkeeper had been an unused substitute for Argentina during their 2-1 defeat to Uruguay on Friday, watching on as Manchester City’s Geronimo Rulli got the nod.

Contrary to reports, Martinez did not don a protective face mask, with his fractured jaw recovered.

Speaking after the game Martinez stated: "The desire is always there. Several things have happened to me lately, and I had to be well because my team-mates need me.”

Martinez’s return to action may represent a selection headache for Alonso ahead of Chelsea’s Premier League clash against Leeds this weekend.

Mike Penders has impressed during the Argentine’s absence, recovering from a shaky performance in Chelsea’s shock 2-0 loss to Tottenham, to prove dependable and stake claim to be the first-choice option in between the sticks.

Penders has already faced Leeds once this season, keeping goal as the Blues roared back from 2-0 down to win 6-3 in the Carabao Cup third round back in September.

However, the 21-year-old’s run of games for Chelsea was not enough to earn a starting role for Belgium during the international break.

Manchester United’s Senne Lammens kept his place as number one for Belgium, as Penders watched on as victories over Turkey and Italy secured a spot in the Nations League quarter finals.

In total, Martinez missed four Premier League games, with Chelsea winning one, drawing the other, and losing twice.

#1816. Manchester United urged to target ‘established Premier League leader’ as Bruno Fernandes replacement

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young has revealed he would replace Bruno Fernandes with Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fernandes's contract expires at the end of this season, though United can extend their captain’s deal by an additional year and also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January about a potential free transfer.

United want Fernandes to stay, but the 32-year-old has already turned down two new contract proposals as he weighs up his options following more managerial turnover at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first training session on Wednesday after leaving the US men’s national team to replace Michael Carrick as United head coach.

Fernandes enjoyed a superb campaign last term, breaking the single-season Premier League assist record to help United qualify for the Champions League.

This season, however, he has struggled to replicate the same form, and he drew criticism after calling into question Carrick’s tactics following United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como in October.

While Young admits there is no doubt about Fernandes’ contribution to United, with the Portuguese midfielder producing 75 goals and 74 assists in 239 Premier League appearances, he insists that in order for the Red Devils to move on, they should look to replace the former Sporting man with England international Gibbs-White.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White.

“I think he's got 18 months left on his contract. He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

No midfielder scored more than Gibbs-White’s 15 Premier League goals last season, with the 26-year-old helping drag Forest clear of the relegation zone.

Young believes a move to United would therefore appeal to Gibbs-White and potentially put him on Tuchel’s radar ahead of the 2028 European Championships.

“I'm sure when he's been away with England as well, you go, and players talk. They'll be talking about the different titles they're going for, the different cups and trophies,” Young continued.

“As a player, you want to play for the biggest clubs in the world. For me, Manchester United is one of those clubs.

“It's going to be down to, obviously, Mauricio Pochettino what he wants to do with Bruno Fernandes. But if you want someone who's properly in their prime, I think Gibbs-White turns 27 next year. I would go after him.”

Young was speaking ahead of the launch of the Panini Official EFL Sticker Collection and said his first memories of collecting the stickers came as a kid at school.

“I always said that, you know, when you used to open packs and get a shiny (sticker), it was the best feeling ever. It was like Christmas come all over again.

“First memories of swapping at school as well. Kids at break time were like, ‘have you got this, have you got that?’ Trying to get the best ones.”

#1815. ‘There are different ways of winning’, says Mead after Man City edge out Hacken

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Beth Mead said "there are different ways to win football matches" after Manchester City battled their way to a 2-0 victory over Hacken.

Man City made it back-to-back wins in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, thanks to second-half goals from Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw.

Andree Jeglertz turned to star attackers Hemp and Shaw at half-time at Nordic Wellness Arena, with City having failed to make the breakthrough in the first period, despite creating chances worth a combined 1.08 expected goals.

Hemp's introduction paid dividends when she opened the scoring in the 55th minute by bundling home while challenging for the ball. She then teed up Shaw to put the result beyond doubt late on, before Mary Fowler missed a stoppage-time penalty.

City finished with 3.43 xG, and while they were not at their clinical best, Mead, who was taken off for Shaw, was more than happy with the performance.

"It was a tough game – we had to work hard for the three points," she told UEFA.

"I'm really proud. It's been a busy schedule. Every player has been bringing different energy to the pitch – a different kind of pitch to play on, obviously. Everybody in the team turned up today and we did what we needed to do.

"There are different ways of winning football matches. Coming away from home in the Champions League is difficult but we found a way to win today."

— Manchester City Women (@ManCityWomen) November 18, 2026

Jeglertz, meanwhile, said City got exactly the game they were expecting.

He told UEFA: "A good game. We knew it would be a tough game to score against a very organised defending team. They have a great goalkeeper and we struggled in first half. In the second half, they got a little bit tired, we got a little more space and we managed to get the goals.

"We try to get the best out of each player and put them in positions where they can really show what qualities they have.

"We have a great team together, we rotate players, and they all have a great impact on what we're doing. I think that will be very important in the future."

City have lost just one of their 11 group stage/league phase games in the Champions League (W6 D3), losing 0-3 to Barcelona in December 2024.

#1814. Chelsea and Manchester United lead tributes as Juan Mata announces football retirement

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea and Manchester United led the tributes to Juan Mata after he announced his retirement from professional football.

The former Spain international, who lifted the 2010 World Cup and 2012 European Championship, has hung up his boots at the age of 38 after leaving Australian giants Melbourne Victory in September.

Mata started his career at Real Madrid’s academy before moving to Valencia in 2007, where he won the 2008 Copa del Rey alongside fellow future World Cup winners David Silva and David Villa.

He moved to Chelsea in 2011 and helped the Blues win the Champions League and FA Cup in his first season at the club. The diminutive midfielder was crowned Chelsea’s Player of the Year in both of his two full seasons in west London before leaving for Manchester United in January 2014.

Mata helped United win the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before his departure in 2022. He then spent the latter years of his career with Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

Mata announced his retirement with a 50-second video posted on his social media channels.

In the video, Mata sits in a changing room, staring at a pair of football boots. He then turns around and hangs them up on a peg, with the caption: “Sometimes to love is to let go. Thanks, football.”

A full statement was also posted on Mata’s official website, in which he admitted “Football will never leave my life” and that he would continue to use football “as a vehicle for development.”

Mata is best known for co-founding Common Goal, a global movement in which players, coaches, and clubs pledge at least 1% of their salaries to fund grassroots football charities.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing. Waking up every morning looking forward to training and playing, whether at magnificent grounds such as Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge or Mestalla.

“Or back when I was starting out at Juventud Estadio, where the pitch turned into a mud bath every winter. I believe that kind of passion is fundamental to everything in life.

“Over time, I realised football was about more than just kicking a ball. As I grew older, travelled and lived in different countries, I came to understand the power of sport in general, and football in particular, to change people’s lives.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.”

Manchester United paid tribute to Mata, who scored 51 goals in 285 games for the Red Devils, with a post on social media.

“Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan,” they wrote on social media.

Chelsea also posted a tribute to Mata on their social media pages.

“What a player,” Chelsea wrote in response to his retirement announcement.

#1812. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1811. England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

Ivan Toney’s bid to move the date of his assault trial to avoid clashing with Euro 2028 games has been refused by a judge.

The England footballer, 30, hopes to be selected to play for the national side in the next European Championship after featuring in this summer’s World Cup .

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6, 2025.

He denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a three- to four-day trial was fixed for June 12, 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

Alleged spy hastened suicide after electronic tag failures, inquest finds

Nations League draw simulated as England get favourable quarter-final tie

Bid to move footballer Ivan Toney’s trial date to avoid Euro 2028 clash refused

‘Bruising’ 7.2% annual fall in inner London house prices is biggest in 17 years

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, which Toney did not attend, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: “It came to our attention that… there may be potentially a football match called the European championships in 2028 between June 9 and July 9.”

Mr Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: “We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

“My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup.”

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a “speculative” application.

He refused the request, saying: “It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed.”

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”.

The Metropolitan Police investigated and the footballer was charged in late July.

Toney, of Northampton, has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country’s Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

#1810. Liverpool make surprise contract U-turn over £55m star as fresh update reveals new Reds 'talks'

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:40

Liverpool have taken a significant step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister's long-term future by opening contract negotiations with the midfielder.

The Argentina international has been keen to extend his stay at Anfield, but there had been growing frustration over the lack of progress.

However, fresh claims suggest the Reds have finally changed their stance and begun discussions over a new deal.

According to reliable Argentine journalist Cesar Luis Merlo (via Sport Witness), Liverpool have opened negotiations with Mac Allister over a contract extension.

The 27-year-old's current agreement runs until June 2028, meaning the Reds have made an early move to keep him at Anfield beyond that date.

There is no agreement in place yet, and Merlo has not disclosed any proposed salary or contract length, although the coming weeks could provide a clearer indication of whether both parties can reach a compromise.

The development represents a change from the situation described by Mac Allister's father and agent, Carlos, who told ESPN Brazil just days ago that Liverpool had not started negotiations.

The long-serving star has also previously voiced his disappointment at the lack of an offer, admitting in September that he was "very, very sad" about the situation, particularly after teammates Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai had been offered new contracts.

More recently, Mac Allister attempted to reassure supporters, expressing hope that the club's board would reconsider its position.

Liverpool's reported change of heart could reflect Mac Allister's importance to Andoni Iraola's plans, with the £55m enforcer continuing to receive regular opportunities.

Starting eight of the Reds' ten Premier League matches and three of their four Champions League fixtures, he remains a prominent part of the team's midfield setup.

That level of involvement makes it difficult to justify allowing uncertainty over his future to continue, particularly when he has consistently indicated a desire to remain at Anfield.

There is still work to do before an agreement is reached, but opening discussions is an encouraging development for Liverpool.

Mac Allister has made his feelings clear, and the club now appears to be responding. Keeping an established midfielder of his importance could prove a sensible decision as Iraola continues shaping his squad.

#1809. Arsenal contract negotiations no longer a major source of stress as transformation complete

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The international break has played out something like an Oprah Winfrey show for the Arsenal squad.

Oprah, back in 2004, marched around her studio, declaring all those in the audience had won a car. Just the 276 Pontiac G6s dished out, for those wondering.

Andrea Berta has seemingly been following that example at Arsenal. “You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!”

It started with the news that Declan Rice had reached an agreement over a new long-term deal, one that will see him join Bukayo Saka on around £350,000-a-week.

Jurrien Timber, too, is set to commit his future to the club. Like Rice, he had entered the final two years of his current deal but the intention was always for Arsenal to tie him down beyond that.

There was more. David Raya has agreed fresh terms as well and will sign a new contract, a year on from receiving a pay rise. This deal will keep him at Arsenal through to 2030.

Piero Hincapie wanted in and is understood to have joined the extension club. The defender only signed for the Gunners permanently in the summer and that deal did not expire until 2031.

However, Hincapie has been rewarded with improved terms for his contribution to the title-winning season and a 12-month extension on the previous deal.

A busy period, then, for those involved in the building and managing of this squad. An extremely indicative one, too, both of how far Arsenal have come and where they want to get to.

It was not that long ago that contract negotiations for key players were a major source of stress for the club.

Under Arsene Wenger, Alexis Sanchez made it clear he had no desire to sign a new deal. Arsenal decided not to sell and he went into the last year of his contract, before joining Manchester United in a swap deal with Henrikh Mkhitaryan.

Terrified of losing Mesut Ozil for free and having been dragged into the final six months of his deal in 2018, Arsenal threw the kitchen sink at him and gave him a £350,000-a-week deal.

For years, Arsenal fans knew exactly when the contracts of the most important players would run out, almost fearing the two years leading up to that.

Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners and more

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in Vinicius talks; Man Utd deal confirmed

Arsenal get new Havertz penalty review as Premier League panel confirm error

Not so now. Rice has entered the final 18 months of his existing deal but there was no real sense of jeopardy. The assumption was always that an extension would be agreed and that has proved correct.

This is now a club that players want to sign but just as crucially want to stay at. Rice’s new deal will commit his prime years to the club, as will be the case with Raya.

You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!

Had Rice wished to explore his options elsewhere, he would have had his pick of the elite clubs across Europe, as would William Saliba before he signed a new deal last year.

Arsenal might not be able to sign the most high-profile players from clubs like Real Madrid, as the summer pursuit of Vinicius Junior showed, but they can now protect their own assets regardless of who wants them.

There are still decisions to be made over other situations. Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz are both out of contract in 2028 as it stands. So too is Ben White and it is understood that as with Odegaard, no contract talks have yet taken place with the club.

However, the dynamic is very different to the one Arsenal have had to put up with in the past. These are not desperate negotiations. If these are players are leave in the transfer windows ahead, it feels like that would be a club-led decision.

These contract extensions also point to the power Mikel Arteta has and the priorities of the club. This is not about building a squad for five or six years down the line. Everything is centred towards giving Arteta the tools to win immediately.

That was apparent in the summer signings of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes, both now 29, and in the handing out of huge contracts to take players well into their 30s.

Arteta has signed a contract of his own through to 2030 and it is all about maximising every opportunity for major trophies between now and then.

His priority is this season and the three beyond it. What happens after that, in terms of the age profile of the squad or the contract situations in the squad, might not be Arteta’s problem.

By then he might be driving off into the sunset. Probably not in a Pontiac G6.

La Liga leaders Barcelona have seen their lead over Real Madrid shrink in recent weeks, with Jose Mourinho’s side now only three points behind after 12 games.
