#1749. Report: €70m Liverpool deal hinges on one major decision

Liverpool have already been linked with a lot of players ahead of the January transfer window.

The Anfield outfit are fourth in the Premier League which, after all the money they've spent, is a massive underperformance.

One of the best ways for the Reds to combat this is to sign new players to plug the gaps their current squad are leaving open.

Obviously, some positions are more of a problem than others with Liverpool likely to have a priority position that they want to strengthen.

But, if they manage to cover all the potential positions they need to, they'll have a massive selection of players to choose from which would obviously be beneficial for them.

Since the Reds aren't a club who have an endless amount of money to spend, their transfers need to mean something which is why their next big deal is hinging on a major decision from the Anfield outfit.

Liverpool are unlikely to sign Lamine Camara in January

Lamine Camara was one of the main players linked with a Liverpool transfer in the summer.

It was clear to almost everyone that a new midfielder was one of the main things that Iraola needed to take the Reds to the next level.

Obviously, replacing Mohamed Salah was also one of the main things that they needed to do but, with how much players such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have struggled to adapt to Iraola's system, the Reds have managed to dig themselves into a bit of a hole.

Because, even though they were desperate for a new midfielder in the summer, by January, it'll be more than clear to every team in the world that a new midfielder is required by the Reds.

In the summer, Camara was available for a cut-rate deal and now, he's worth around €70 million.

The fact of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch also having prominent roles among their ranks also needs to be taken into consideration as, if another midfielder is brought in, the minutes played by each player will diminish.

And, according to David Lynch via Anfield Index, this could be the thing to stop them from signing the Senegal international.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he said.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a question of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know."

Lamine Camara would be a perfect transfer for Liverpool

Before the summer, Camara was probably a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The midfielder was quietly making a name for himself in Ligue 1 and then, when Filipe Luis took over as their manager, he instantly became one of the first names on their team sheet.

From that point on, clubs from across the world were interested in the midfielder and have remained so ever since.

But, of all the teams he's been linked with, Liverpool are the team he'd be perfect for.

Not only would he perfectly fit into Iraola's plans but, he'd also be able to come in for one of his starting midfielders.

Indeed, the €70 million fee is a bit of a risk but, in reality, that's the going rate for a decent central midfielder these days.

Here's hoping that Liverpool come to their senses and get a deal over the line.

#1748. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

Liverpool can move forward with a transfer after Barcelona named their price for the player. The ball is firmly in the Reds' court now.

Liverpool need a new left-back. That much is abundantly clear to everyone and it’s something that will inevitably happen in 2027 - it’s just a matter of when.

They might move in January, depending on how Andoni Iraola views the current squad. It’s clear he’s not enamoured with either Milos Kerkez or Kostas Tsimikas by the way he’s constantly rotating the pair.

Kerkez, though, is here for the long term. Liverpool invested in him and he’s still so young - there’s zero reason to write him off at this stage and we’re still confident that he’ll make it at Anfield.

However, Tsimikas’s contract expires next summer and we see no real chance that he gets a new one. Liverpool will have to find competition for Kerkez, both to give him a reason to keep pushing and to hedge the bets here.

Liverpool, after all, are far more likely to find an elite left-back if they’re investing in two, rather than going all-in on Kerkez.

Barcelona set Alex Balde priceBarcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus. Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Barcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus.

Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Liverpool are also interested in Balde. The player wasn't keen on leaving Catalonia back in the summer but things have reportedly changed. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has held tentative talks with the Reds, supposedly.

The door is now open, then. A deal with the Reds has room to move forward with Barcelona's price now known and the real question is whether Liverpool actually want to pay that.

It's essentially what they paid for Kerkez and the idea of having two left-backs worth over €40m does seem a bit mad. Especially when so many other areas of the squad require consideration and probably investment.

Balde, though, may be as sure of a thing as Liverpool can get at that price point. One thing's for sure - it'll tempt them.

#1745. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery 'interested' in midfielder with 155 Chelsea appearances

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 12:53

Aston Villa have reportedly identified AC Milan midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek as a potential winter transfer target.

Earlier on Wednesday, Villa announced that one of their current engine-room options had penned a new long-term contract.

Unai Emery is also not short of players for that position, with Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka and Ross Barkley earning regular minutes.

Nevertheless, not helped by the inconsistent performances and individual mistakes of some of those aforementioned players, Villa remain off the pace in the Premier League.

According to Calciomercato, Loftus-Cheek has emerged as a possible option for the turn of the year.

The report alleges that Villa Park is viewed as a 'potential destination' for the former Chelsea midfielder.

Loftus-Cheek contributed 13 goals and 18 assists from his 155 appearances in a Blues shirt, but he has been at San Siro since the summer of 2023.

His stint at AC Milan can be viewed as a relative success, with 13 goals and four assists coming from 109 outings for the Italian giants.

However, the 11-cap England international's contract is due to expire at the end of the season, putting him in a position where he could leave on a free transfer in the summer.

Milan are open to cashing in on the 30-year-old in order to free up transfer funds and space on their wage bill.

Ruben Amorim's side have also won their last two matches against Inter Milan and Genoa, games which Loftus-Cheek missed through injury.

Despite Loftus-Cheek possessing qualities that Emery arguably lacks within his squad, a move to Villa makes little sense for the player.

Villa already have too many options in the number six, eight and 10 positions in Emery's familiar 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-1-1 formations.

Although Tammy Abraham has been linked with an exit from Villa, it seems unlikely that Loftus-Cheek would transition into a backup number nine behind Nicolas Jackson and Brian Madjo at this point of his career.

#1744. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

#1743. Opinion: Andoni Iraola forced to sacrifice 95-goal Liverpool star to sign €70m midfielder

Andoni Iraola has tried his best to turn Liverpool's fortunes around at Anfield since his arrival.

Last term, the club were performing well below expectations and ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League.

In a normal season, managing to qualify for the Champions League would be seen as a decent outcome but, after spending £450 million on new players and winning the title just a season before, it was a bad performance.

Their lack of form resulted in Arne Slot being sacked and left Iraola to deal with all of his shortcomings.

Most of the time, things have gone well but, for them to get even better, changes are going to have to take place in the upcoming transfer window.

Liverpool would have to sell Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch to sign Lamine Camara

Liverpool's midfield has been one of their main problems since 2023.

The July of 2023 was when Fabinho exited Anfield and, since then, the Reds haven't had a natural number six among their ranks.

Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have all been used there to try and plug the gap.

And, while Gravenberch did fairly well during the Reds' title-winning season, from that point on, he's failed to meet expectations.

That's why in the 2026-27 summer transfer window, fans were sure that a new number six would be brought in.

Obviously, Richard Hughes and Iraola didn't feel the need to do that, even though the Spaniard's double pivot has been the thing to cause them the most issues so far.

Several different players were linked as potential options for the Reds to explore but, according to an update from David Lynch via Anfield Index, the Reds would have to sell Gravenberch or Szoboszlai to make room for someone such as Lamine Camara.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he said.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a questions of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know."

Liverpool would have to spend around €70m to sign Lamine Camara

Before the 2026-27 season got fully underway, Liverpool were heavily linked with Camara.

In fact, some outlets were even reporting that a deal for the Senegal international was going to be done before the end of the transfer window.

That obviously never ended up happening and now, they're being linked once again with the form of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch raising a fair few questions.

But, for the Reds to sign Camara, it's been reported that a fee worth around €70 million would have to be spent for AS Monaco to even think about letting him go.

Since they rejected his move to Chelsea during the dying embers of the window, he's gone from strength to strength and now, the Ligue 1 outfit are seeing that he's worth a lot of money.

Right now, nothing is decided but, sacrificing someone such as Szoboszlai feels like a big leap, especially for an unproven player in the Premier League.

#1742. AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:59

The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

With four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

The last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.

One by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX

While waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

#1741. Deal complete: Chelsea owners steal in before Liverpool's FSG

Chelsea's owners, Blue Co., have swooped in to steal a deal ahead of Liverpool and FSG. This wasn't how things were supposed to go.

Everything changed at Liverpool in early 2024 as Jurgen Klopp got ready to leave the club. The German's exit provided an opportunity for an overhaul - and a move towards a new plan.

Liverpool's owners FSG welcomed back Michael Edwards and Julian Ward, installing Richard Hughes as sporting director. Edwards and Ward, however, weren't strictly working for Liverpool but instead headed up a new multi-club project.

Multi-club projects, while correctly controversial, are an increasingly common occurrence in football as elite clubs look to consolidate their position. FSG wanted a piece of that and instructed Edwards to help lead the search for more clubs to bring under their ownership.

The idea, however, fell flat. FSG consistently failed to find a club for a reasonable price and eventually cancelled the plan around two and half years after kicking it off.

Blue Co. sign Vitor MatosSwansea City coach Vitor Matos has, per Fabrizio Romano, agreed to take over at Strasbourg. The French side are owned by Chelsea's owners Blue Co. and they'll now take the highly-rated coach under their wing. Swansea have been enjoying life under Matos and it's no surprise that he's been given a 'bigger' gig. However, this was supposed to be FSG making the move.

Swansea City coach Vitor Matos has, per Fabrizio Romano, agreed to take over at Strasbourg. The French side are owned by Chelsea's owners Blue Co. and they'll now take the highly-rated coach under their wing.

Swansea have been enjoying life under Matos and it's no surprise that he's been given a 'bigger' gig. However, this was supposed to be FSG making the move.

Matos, after all, was one of Klopp's assistants at Liverpool and only left the Reds when the German did. He embarked on a career as a head coach but Sunday Times correspondent Jonathan Northcroft claims the plan was always to bring him 'back'.

'Back' meaning to a club under the FSG flag, in other words. Matos was viewed as one for the future and someone who could help lead the development at a different club. You'd imagine the potential for him to rejoin Liverpool as head coach was there, too.

Instead, it's the Chelsea group who've got him. Matos is heading there with Strasbourg and it feels as though the Reds have missed their chance.

#1740. Hutchinson admits ‘dream’ is to be bought by Milan and insists Scudetto is possible

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

Hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more important one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

“They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

“In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

“No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”

#1738. Bayern Munich vs FC Koln - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 13:05

Bayern Munich can take a lead in the race for the Bundesliga title on Friday, when they welcome FC Koln to Allianz Arena.

The hosts are level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who play on Saturday, whereas Koln are 15th with nine points after nine matchweeks.

Prior to the start of the November international break, Bayern emerged as 2-1 victors against Mainz 05, though they were wasteful in the final third, missing three of their four big chances while scoring just two of their 26 shots.

That win was their fourth in five games in all competitions, but it will be a concern that the team have only kept one clean sheet in their last eight matches.

The Bavarians have conceded 17 goals in their 16 fixtures this season, whereas they only conceded 13 times in the corresponding period in 2025-26.

Fans will hope the expected return of Vincent Kompany, who has not been in the dugout for his side's last five fixtures since collapsing on October 23, will help boost the team's performances at the back.

Bayern have drawn two of their three most recent contests at Allianz Arena, though they are yet to experience defeat at home, winning five of their seven clashes when playing as hosts.

Kompany's side have averaged five goals per game at home in the Bundesliga, while they only conceded four goals in their four league outings at Allianz Arena.

Koln were beaten 2-1 by Bayer Leverkusen on November 8 before the start of the international break, and it will concern supporters that the club have now won just one of their past eight top-flight games (W1, D4, L3).

Manager Rene Wagner will want his team to improve considerably in the final third given they have netted just twice in their last four league fixtures, blanking on two occasions.

A defeat on Friday would leave the visitors as low as 17th should Union Berlin and Schalke 04 claim three points in matchday 10, though it should be noted that only three points separate them from eighth-placed Stuttgart.

The Billy Goats' record against Bayern is predictably poor, with Wagner's side last beating their hosts in February 2011, and another loss would be their 22nd defeat in 24 meetings.

Koln's solitary victory in their five away matches this campaign came in the DFB-Pokal against Wurzburger Kickers in August, and they have since lost three games and settled for a stalemate once.

Bayern's injuries are still extensive despite the break from football, with left-back Alphonso Davies (hamstring) and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer (foot), as well as attackers Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring), among those to miss out.

Jonas Urbig will feature between the posts, while Josip Stanisic is almost certain to be stationed at left-back, with Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah set to start as centre-backs.

In the forward line, Ballon d'or-winner Harry Kane may play ahead of a supporting cast consisting of Lennart Karl, Michael Olise and Nathaniel Brown.

Koln are also dealing with several injury issues, especially in defence considering both Timo Hubers and Rav van den Berg will be absent.

Joel Schmied, Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and Tom Krauss are the likely trio to start in the visitors' back three, while the club's attacking efforts will be led by forwards Marius Bulter and Said El Mala.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Karl, Olise, Brown; Kane

Schwabe; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Maina, Okon-Engstler, Johannesson, Sosa; Bulter, El Mala

Bayern Munich have shown that they are far from flawless at the back in recent months, so there should be openings for Koln.

However, the Bavarians have continued to be irresistible in attack despite their injuries, and they should be able to get the better of the visitors.

#1736. Report: 'Incredible' Premier League defender eyed by Liverpool, it's his dream

Liverpool have been linked with many different players over the years.

However, their last couple have consisted of the most spending that they've ever done.

Around £600 million has been splashed on new players by Liverpool and, there are still a lot more areas among their ranks that could do with an upgrade or two.

Right now, it's unclear what their main priorities are but, since they're fourth in the Premier League and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal, it's clear that change is needed.

Obviously, big deals don't often get completed in January but, if Iraola wants to give his men the best chance possible this term, some big transfers are going to have to be agreed.

Liverpool are eyeing up a move for Josko Gvardiol

Right now, left-back is probably one of Liverpool's main problem areas.

Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas have both failed to meet expectations with neither of them managing to prove their worth.

Of course, the former of the two is still young so he still has a lot of his career ahead of him but, since he's their first choice, you'd have expected a lot more from him.

Links with left-backs such as Alejandro Balde and Julian Ryerson have emerged but, thanks to an update from El Nacional CAT, an even better option has entered the discussion.

"Barcelona are calmly considering the possibility of trying to sign Gvardiol, although this would involve a significant investment," they wrote.

"The Sky Blues won't let go of a player for whom they paid over €90 million, making him one of the most expensive defenders of all time. Nor will they allow him to leave mid-season, so they would have to wait until the summer transfer window.

"Furthermore, there is another obstacle that makes it extremely difficult to see the former Dinamo Zagreb and RB Leipzig player at the Spotify Camp Nou, and for him to be available to Hans-Dieter Flick.

"There will be a lot of competition for Gvardiol The situation surrounding Gvardiol and City has attracted the attention of many clubs , who are willing to try their luck and fight for his signing.

"For example, he has been linked with Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool, Bayern Munich, Chelsea, and Al-Nassr. In other words, Barça will face several rivals in the fight to secure his services."

Josko Gvardiol's dream move has always been Liverpool

Before Manchester City jumped in and prised Josko Gvardiol away from RB Leipzig, the Croatian always spoke about how it was his dream to join Liverpool.

There have been several interviews where the "incredible" defender has shared that the team he supports is Liverpool.

His favoured position is obviously centre-back but, with the Reds still having now idea what they're doing with that area of their squad, he could come in as another option at left-back for Liverpool.

Not only would this help shore up Iraola's defence like Ronald Araujo has but, it would also give Kerkez someone to properly compete against.

Of course, the window isn't open yet so deals can't be struck right now but, the fact that Gvardiol has re-entered Liverpool's thinking is excellent news.

Arsenal secured another away win last night, this time in the Champions League beating Slavia Prague 2-1 thanks to goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres.

Mikel Arteta rotated in some areas, with starts for Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze, but relied too on the foundational stability of Declan Rice with Ezri Konsa and Gabriel behind him. We began in lively fashion, and took an early lead.

David Raya played it long, Gyokeres held it up well and hooked the ball forward, and Madueke’s pace took him beyond the defender and into the box before finishing between the keeper’s legs. Solid play from two players who can sometimes be guilty of fluffing their lines when it comes to those key actions. This time they were spot on.

We had more chances to score. Eze showed nice skills in the box but saw his shot blocked; Gyokeres headed back across goal for Merino but he headed over; the Spaniard saw a shot from distance tipped over, and his smart near post run and a right-footed shot from a Ben White cutback forced the keeper into another decent stop; and there was a brilliant counter and pass from Rice that drifted all the way to the back post without any Arsenal player attacking it for a tap-in.

We did find a second though. Gyokeres combined well with Merino around their box, and when he was played through he opened up his body really well and produced a fine finish from close range and a tight angle to make it 2-0. I don’t think that goal at Fleetwood would have done much for his confidence, this felt much more like the kind of strike he needed to produce – for himself as much as the team.

So, we had a good lead at the break, but this was very much a game of two halves. In the first we had 60% possession, out-shot the opposition by 8 to 2, and passed at nearly 90% success rate. In the second, the tables turned. Slavia Prague took 17 shots to our 4, and our pass success fell to 77%. We were sloppy and untidy, they made a tactical change at half-time which worked well for them, and while we weren’t necessarily under the cosh, the entire dynamic of the game changed and we couldn’t get to grips with it.

We needed David Raya to make one superb save to keep them at bay, before Gabriel had to head one off the line, but in injury time they found the goal I think their second half performance (and ours) probably merited. They whipped in a wicked ball from the left, the striker applied the close range finish, and the clean sheet was gone.

Afterwards, Mikel Arteta was happy with the win, but displeased with the second half, saying:

First of all, you have to value the fact it’s very difficult to win away from home. We’ve done it against a very tough opponent, we expected that toughness. In the first half we played at a really high level in terms of intensity, tempo, quality and clarity in what we had to do, and what the game was demanding. We were very efficient – we should have scored three, four or five.

I already talked about some of the things we didn’t do, and others I’d prefer not to mention. It’s a huge lesson, and we’ll learn from the second half. It’s our third away game in quick succession, and we’re the only team to have played three away games in the Champions League and just one at home – there are a lot of factors – but I don’t like to use that, because in the first half we were at the level we wanted. I take full responsibility for the drop in the second half.

I don’t think the team played well at all in the second half, but I do wonder about how we might have done things differently. For example, I feel like Declan Rice played within himself in that second period, and let me be clear, I understand why. Personally, I think it’s a bit mad he did 90+ minutes in a game like this, even if I accept he and the manager know more about his fitness than any of us. Maybe they need him to be like a steam train, going going going all the time, but when you have options of the quality of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes on the bench, surely using them in his stead allows the best of two worlds: some rest for Rice, and fresher legs in midfield when the game is tilting in the opposition’s favour.

We have this really strong bench, but I don’t think the changes we made worked particularly well. The question, of course, is if they absolutely needed to. We had a two goal lead until late on, and we secured all three points away from home after a difficult and physically demanding game at Anfield three days previously. I just found the Jekyll and Hyde nature of of the two halves a little concerning, but only a little. Ten of our sixteen games this season have been away from home, we’ve won seven of them, so that’s a decent return, added to by this victory.

Ultimately, this is essentially a forgettable Champions League tie that we came away with three points from. Apparently it was a year to the day since we played Slavia Prague last season too, a game I had/have zero recollection of. Which might say something about me more than anything else, but these kinds of fixtures don’t live long in the memory. They’re grist for the mill in this part of the season, we had a job to do, and we got it done, and now all the focus turns to Hull on Saturday and the three points required there before the Interlull.

We can talk a bit more about this game in an Arsecast a bit later on this morning, before I head to London a bit later on this afternoon. For those who have registered to come to the launch of The 22 tomorrow at Big Red, please remember you can purchase the book via the email sent to you (check your junk folders if you don’t see it), so you can simply come and collect on the night. We can also facilitate sales via credit card etc if you don’t want to do that.

If you purchased via the Patreon pre-sale, those books are not for collection tomorrow, and will be shipped to you in due course. There is also some scope to come along on spec on the night, and we should have copies available but obviously priority goes to those who registered. We will then have a final batch of books going on general sale online on Saturday evening after the Hull game. Full details of that to follow here on site and via Arseblog on BlueSky.

Ok, I’ll leave it there for now. Pod will be out mid-morning, until then, have a good one.
